blueprint.purpose: Make sure no growth team is ever bottlenecked on knowing what ads to run next.
blueprint.explainer: An AI agent for creative briefs that learns from your ad results.
blueprint.positioning_statement: For heads of growth at DTC brands spending $50k to $1M+ a month on Meta, who are bottlenecked on knowing what ads to run next, Yolodex is the AI creative strategy team that finds the winning angles and builds the shoot-ready briefs, then learns from every ad result. Unlike a generic-AI stack, an agency, or another strategist hire, Yolodex is purpose-built for creative strategy and closes the loop from brief to live ad to read-back.

promise.headline: Creative is the new targeting.
promise.subline: We build the creative briefs that win.
promise.rationale: Meta's Andromeda-era ranking makes creative the targeting. The brand that finds better ideas faster grows faster. The bottleneck is no longer production, it is knowing what to run.

enemy.smaller_brands: Guessing with taste. A strategist (or founder) with opinions and no experiment.
enemy.bigger_brands: The generic-AI stack (Claude/ChatGPT + Motion/Foreplay). Rob Snyder's line: the nerdiest PhD who follows instructions and whose output is garbage every time, because it has no creative intuition and never learns from results.

audience.primary_buyer: Head of Growth / Performance at a DTC brand
tried_before: hiring a creative strategist who still can't keep up

blueprint.proof_style: Show the machine. Explain the models, the loop, and the evidence behind every brief. Transparency is the trust signal, backed by named-brand numbers.

hero_story.setup: Hit a creative wall. Couldn't scale briefs even with AI.
hero_story.ideal_quote: We 10x'd our briefing output without increasing the workload on our creative strategists, and improved our win rate. Yolodex briefs now account for 90% of our winning ads.

supporting_proof.stat: 15 briefs in the time it used to take to make 2. A Yolodex-briefed static is their current top-spend ad.
~$1M of briefed spend. Roughly 40% of winning ad concepts originated by Yolodex.
Cohort nCPA £35 against a £35 target, bang on for the first time.

blueprint.ambition: Category creator, anti-SaaS. Look and sound nothing like the AI-creative-tool pack.

voice.register: British, plain, very confident. Not understated: Yolodex states what it does and what the numbers are, and does not hedge.
rules: Lead with the claim, then the evidence. Never the other way round.
Every claim carries a number, a name, or a mechanism.
No exclamation marks in marketing copy. Confidence comes from specifics, not punctuation.
Contractions are fine. First person plural (we), second person (you).
Name real brands and real people wherever we have permission.
Explain the machine in plain words. If a reader can't picture how it works, rewrite.
banned_words: 10x (as a verb in copy; fine as a stat)

team.concept: Yolodex is an AI creative strategy team. Each agent maps to a real job on an in-house creative strategy team so a head of growth instantly understands what it replaces or multiplies.

lead.name: Yolo Badger
lead.does: Ranks where to play, decides what runs next, hands out the work, reports back in plain English. The in-app voice of the product and the brand mascot.

agents.title: Creative Analyst
agents.does: Takes every ad apart frame by frame and tags hook, format, pacing, talent, music, claim.

agents.title: Performance Analyst
agents.does: Reads Meta results and isolates which variables actually drove the win.

agents.title: Insights Researcher
agents.does: Mines reviews, Reddit, ad comments and surveys for the language customers actually use.

agents.title: Creative Researcher
agents.does: Scouts competitor and category ads and builds the reference board for each brief.

agents.title: Creative Strategist
agents.does: Turns persona × angle × evidence into a shoot-ready brief.

agents.title: Copywriter
agents.does: Writes the hooks, scripts and on-screen text for every brief.

agents.title: Experimentation Lead
agents.does: Designs the sprint test plan and closes the loop when the ads go live.

team.graphic: An org chart drawn like a newspaper masthead: Yolo Badger on top, seven bylines beneath, each with a one-line job description. Used on the homepage, the deck and the /brand page.

usage: Always 'Yolodex', never 'the Yolodex' or 'YOLODEX' in running text.
Say 'your AI creative strategy team' in the first sentence of any new context, then just 'Yolodex'.

retire: Creative Scientist™ (as the category label; may survive as an internal nickname only)
opportunity matrix (rename to 'where to play' in customer-facing copy)

naming.agents: Capitalised job titles: Creative Analyst, Performance Analyst, Insights Researcher, Creative Researcher, Creative Strategist, Copywriter, Experimentation Lead. Team lead: Yolo Badger.
taglines_shortlist: Creative is the new targeting. We build the creative briefs that win.
Never be bottlenecked on what ads to run.
10x the briefs. Same team. Higher win rate.

visual.line: Editorial, pushed hard away from the competitor set. Paper ground, ink type, one signal colour, real ads with the machine's markup on them. The competitor set is dark-mode SaaS with purple/blue/green gradients; Yolodex looks like the research desk of a serious publication.

signature_device.name: Annotated ads
signature_device.description: Real customer ads with Yolodex's markup over them: tags, hairline callouts, variable labels and evidence notes in mono type and the signal colour. 'Show the machine' made visual. No competitor shows their working on the ad itself.

logo.direction: Two-part system. (1) The mark: Yolo Badger's head, front-on, round glasses, cream face with charcoal stripes. This is the favicon, app icon and Slack icon from day one. (2) The wordmark: lowercase 'yolodex' in the body grotesk, tight tracking. Lock-up is mark left, wordmark right. The wordmark can stand alone on long-form pages; the mark stands alone at small sizes.

badger.status: Existing character. Chubby, upright, round wire glasses, cream face and belly, charcoal coat with a cream stripe over the head, pink nose, thick eyebrows. Warm and a bit bookish. The glasses carry the Scientist archetype.
renditions: Full character (colour, soft cartoon line): in-app moments, empty states, onboarding, the team masthead, social.
Head mark (simplified, 2-colour: ink + paper, optional signal-colour circle behind): favicon 16/32/48px, app icon, Slack, OG corner.
Line version (single-weight ink outline, no fill): editorial pages, print, stamps and footers.
rules: Never stretch, recolour or add gradients.
Keep the glasses in every rendition; they are the recognition feature at small sizes.
The character is the team lead, so it can speak in first person in-app. It never appears in customer case-study imagery.

avoid: stock photos of people at laptops

palettes.name: Marker yellow
palettes.notes: Highlighter on paper. 'Marked as winner.' Bullish and optimistic. Nobody in AI creative tooling uses it. Yellow is a highlight colour only: never set text in it, set text on it.

palettes.name: Salmon paper
palettes.notes: The ground is the colour, the accent is ink. Financial Times move. Instantly recognisable, reads as serious business press. Rare in SaaS.

palettes.name: Oxblood
palettes.notes: Grown-up, expensive, editorial. Warm rather than techy. Risk: old-money rather than bullish.

palettes.name: Cobalt
palettes.notes: Scientific and punchy on cream paper. Klein-blue energy. Risk: blue is the B2B default, though this shade on paper is not.

type_pairings.name: Instrument
type_pairings.notes: Sharp editorial serif for display, tight grotesk for UI and body, mono for annotations and data. Modern, confident, not delicate.

type_pairings.name: Fraunces
type_pairings.notes: Characterful soft serif with optical sizes. Warmer, more personality, slightly less serious.

type_pairings.name: Newsreader
type_pairings.notes: Newspaper-derived serif. The most 'press' feeling. Pairs with masthead layouts.

layout: Generous margins, hairline rules, a real column grid.
Big serif display, small mono captions with the source under every number.
Numbers are set in the display serif. Sources in mono.
Light by default. A dark 'machine' section is allowed for product screenshots and diagrams only.
Yellow (or the chosen signal) is used like a highlighter: underline swipes, tags, one hero block. Never more than ~10% of any composition.
imagery: Real customer ads, always annotated. Never a naked screenshot.
Real product and packaging photography from customers, with permission.
Diagrams: single-weight line drawings, ink on paper, mono labels.
No stock photography of any kind.
Illustration: Yolo Badger (see logo.badger for the three renditions) and single-weight technical diagrams. Nothing else.

phase_1: Yolo Badger head mark (SVG: full colour, ink-on-paper, paper-on-ink) at favicon/app-icon sizes
Wordmark (SVG, ink and paper versions) and mark + wordmark lock-up
LinkedIn post template (annotated ad + one stat)
